title: Single-Consumer Assumption in Multi-Consumer Queue
pattern: Using a single-producer/single-consumer (SPSC) queue or stack implementation with multiple concurrent consumers.
why_bad: SPSC algorithms omit atomic serialization (like CAS) on the dequeue/enqueue paths to maximize performance. If multiple consumers access the dequeue path concurrently, they will execute overlapping instructions, resulting in torn pointers, lost elements, and severe memory corruption.
detection: A non-atomic collection dequeue method accessed concurrently by multiple threads without an external coordinating lock.
counterexample: Guarding the SPSC queue with a Mutex when using it in a multi-consumer context.
fix: Wrap SPSC queue accesses in a lock, or use a Multi-Producer Multi-Consumer (MPMC) queue.
